evidence.excerpt: Classifiers deployed in production legal systems regularly encounter documents that belong to no category in the training taxonomy—newly enacted law types, atypical procedural forms, or documents from adjacent domains. This paper studies out-of-distribution (OOD) detection as a complement to standard closed-set classification in the context of Serbian administrative law. Seven OOD detection methods are evaluated: maximum softmax probability, ODIN, Mahalanobis distance, energy-based scoring, a Monte Carlo dropout ensemble, a deep ensemble, and a one-class neural baseline. Evaluation uses an in-distribution set of 6,400 administrative decisions across 16 categories and four OOD sets of increasing distance from the in-distribution. At a 95% true-positive rate threshold, energy-based scoring and the Mahalanobis method perform best, achieving AUROC values of 0.91 and 0.89 respectively. The paper discusses calibration of classifier confidence scores as a prerequisite for reliable OOD thresholding in production deployments.
